notes: Holt's notes on arms (training level A5, D-59): advice in the world, not a recipe system. Every attempt is still judged and nothing is keyed to these words.
title: Sergeant Holt's Notes on Arms
intro: Thirty years in the Duke's companies, and what I learned of making do. Most of it is: use what's lying about, and do it in the right order.
A good weapon starts as a good tool. Grind before you haft; soak hide before you bind.

recipes.name: A spearhead from a broken blade
steps: Grind the broken end to a point on the grindstone, keeping it wet from the trough.
Grind both edges back from the point, so it cuts as well as stabs.
Leave a stub of tang to seat in the haft.
recipes.say: grind the broken sword blade to a sharp spear point on the grindstone, keeping it wet
recipes.good_for: The head of a spear. Useless on its own without a haft.

recipes.name: Hafting a spear
steps: Split the end of the pole a hand's length and seat the tang in it.
Soak the rawhide in the trough till it's soft.
Bind it tight round the split; it shrinks as it dries and grips like iron.
recipes.say: seat the spearhead in the split end of the ash pole and bind it tight with soaked rawhide
recipes.good_for: Reach. Keep them off you; a spear wins more fights than a sword.

recipes.name: A quilted jack
steps: Cut the linen into a front, a back and sleeves, two layers each.
Stuff wool between the layers, thick as your thumb.
Quilt it in rows a finger apart so the stuffing can't slip.
recipes.say: cut the linen into two layers, stuff the wool between them and quilt it into a padded jack
recipes.good_for: Turns a glancing cut and softens a club. Hot to wear.

recipes.name: A buckler
steps: Lay the boards edge to edge and cut a round from them.
Soak the rawhide and bind the rim, crossing on the back for a grip.
recipes.say: cut a round buckler from the oak boards and bind its rim with soaked rawhide
recipes.good_for: A small shield for the left fist: knock blows aside.

recipes.name: On the dummy
steps: Put it on; take it up.
Go at the dummy as if it meant you harm.
If it holds and bites, it'll do. If it doesn't, better to learn it on straw.
recipes.say: thrust my spear into the straw dummy to test it
